newsitem.title: CHILE: Chilean legislators seek top judge's impeachment.
newsitem.headline: Chilean legislators seek top judge's impeachment.

text.p: A group of Chilean congressmen formally called for the impeachment of the country's Supreme Court president on Tuesday in a widening scandal over alleged drug corruption in the courts.

Ten rightist legislators accused court president Servando Jordan of overstepping his authority in three drug trafficking cases, including one in which he allegedly tried to slow down the prosecution of the accused leader of a money-laundering scheme.
In another case, Jordan was one of five judges who ordered the release on bail in 1991 of an alleged Colombian cocaine trafficker in Santiago without the man's lawyer filing a bail request.
Jordan has denied any wrongdoing. He declined on Tuesday to comment on the accusation.

"This is a motion against the influence of drug trafficking in our judicial system," one of the legislators, Carlos Bombal, told reporters after filing the charges in Congress, which meets in the port of Valparaiso.

All 10 lawmakers were from the rightist Independent Democratic Union (UDI) party. Leaders of other parties including those in President Eduardo Frei's centre-left coalition said they may support the accusation against Jordan and may file charges against other top judges.
If the Chamber of Deputies approves the measure, Jordan would be immediately suspended from his post. He would be removed from office if the charges were later approved by the Senate, after hearings.
Chile has so far been spared most of the violence and corruption associated with the drugs trade in some of its South American neighbours.

But Chileans have been shaken by the case of alleged money-launderer Mario Silva Leiva, known as "the Horse Racing Kid" because of his fondness for betting on horse races, accused of handling millions of dollars in drug money and assembling a vast protection ring in the courts.
